entry_orbs.why: The panel gives an independent Visible Alpha-consensus cross-check (with a stated vendor error margin) on AWS/Azure/GCP 1Q26 growth that the current guidance-consensus read does not carry.

The panel's AWS/cloud growth estimate and AI-token-share detail sit below the granularity of the run's current Q1 2026 10-Q-based revenue-driver read and directly speak to revenue-drivers' WHAT-TO-READ (alt-data panels, cloud growth decomposition).
The AI-token-share swing (AWS 16%->51%, Azure 53%->27% y/y) is competitive-economics evidence bearing on moat's AWS-vs-Azure-vs-GCP competitive-position read.

summary: Eleven documents have landed since the 2026-07-10 run's watermark: one tier-5 YipitData cloud-spend panel (unchanged and still unactioned since 2026-07-23) and ten tier-10 screener wire events, two of which are new since the 2026-07-29 scan. The YipitData panel still clears the materiality gate (68) with an independent Visible Alpha-consensus cross-check and AI-token-share detail, so the scoped rerun (earnings/guidance-consensus, earnings/revenue-drivers, business-model/moat, and cascade) stands unchanged and still has not been executed. Of the ten wire events, none clears the gate for an immediate rerun: most re-report Q1 2026 earnings-call figures or third-party surveys already reflected in the thesis, one reports a scale-immaterial facility closure, and one reports an unconfirmed external Trainium chip-sales rumor. The most consequential new item is a single-sourced report of a $25B Amazon bond issuance to fund AI data-center capex (EVT-f28b09ba4feb) — material and quantified, but tier-10 single-source per INTAKE.md §5, so it is note_only pending a confirming filing or second independent source.
